_comment: Tier-2 for fourc::multiscale#5, executed in RVE COUNTS and never in seconds — no clock is read anywhere in this fixture. Upstream sohex8_multiscale_macro.4C.yaml is 8 hex8 macro elements with 8 Gauss points each, every Gauss point carrying its own MAT_Struct_Multiscale RVE, so 64 RVE solves per macro Newton step, each performed by whichever rank owns the macro element. 4C writes that ownership itself as the element_owner cell array of its structure runtime VTK output, and reading it back gives: 1 rank -> a single queue of 64; 2 ranks -> 3 and 5 elements, queues of 24 and 40; 3 ranks -> 1, 3 and 4 elements, queues of 8, 24 and 32, a four-to-one spread on a mesh whose perfect split would be 2-3-3. The spread is not transient: the element_owner map at the last output step is byte-identical to the one at the first in every arm, so nothing is redistributed while the run proceeds, which is exactly the entry's point. And all three runs exit 0 with zero result-test failures, so the imbalance never shows up in the answer — counting who owns what is the only way to see it. Verified by execution 2026-08-06 against 4C at /home/alexander/4C/build/4C with OpenMPI.

_mutation.note: remove the pathology: run the three-rank arm on a single rank instead, so no macro decomposition and no queue imbalance can arise. ELEMENTS_PER_RANK_NP3 becomes 8, RVE_QUEUE_NP3 becomes 64, MIN_RVE_QUEUE_NP3 becomes 64 and RVE_QUEUE_IMBALANCE_NP3 becomes 1.00, so the fixture must go red.
remove the pathology from the two-rank arm as well: on one rank ELEMENTS_PER_RANK_NP2 becomes 8, RVE_QUEUE_NP2 becomes 64 and RVE_QUEUE_IMBALANCE_NP2 becomes 1.00, so the fixture must go red.
